owned_invariants: Each entry hash is SHA-256 of the domain line and the JSON of (seq, prev, record); replay refuses any edit, reorder or gap as CHAIN_BROKEN.
A failure is typed by the canon (failure class, DDC letters) and binds a 64-hex evidence hash.
A candidate rule must cite recorded failures. Its trial must be held out: no held-out id may name the case of a failure the rule came from, where the case of an id is the part before its first @.
A rule is admitted only while it is a candidate whose latest trial beat the baseline with zero hits on clean work; retirement is final.
admitted() lists exactly the rules a later run may load.
head() is the hash of the last entry, or the genesis value for an empty ledger, and names that state of the ledger.
at(head) rebuilds the ledger as it stood at that head by replaying its first entries; a hash no entry has is refused as UNKNOWN_LEDGER_HEAD.
on_trial(id) returns a rule only while it is proposed or rejected; an admitted or retired rule is refused as NOT_ON_TRIAL.
boundaries: The ledger records what a host reports; it does not run the trial itself.
Counts are compared, not combined, so there is no arithmetic to overflow.
The case of an id is read from the id. Ids the host writes from stored turns (turns.rs) name the case by content; an id a caller chose is taken at its word.
